title: Habitat fragmentation as a driver of species decline — Red List assessments overview
claim: Habitat fragmentation is repeatedly identified across IUCN Red List species assessments as a major threat driving population decline, independent of overall habitat area lost.
evidence_text: IUCN Red List threat classification data consistently records habitat fragmentation — the breaking of continuous habitat into smaller, disconnected patches — as a distinct threat from outright habitat loss, and one strongly associated with declining population trends across taxa. This supports prioritising connectivity-focused restoration (corridors, stepping-stone patches, buffer zones) even in landscapes where some habitat area remains, particularly where field observations already indicate reduced species activity.
